first_summary:
The rot in workflow-patterns.md is concentrated in four places. The old 1x/2x/4-5x/10x output ladder (line 121), the "Haiku accepts none" effort claim (line 30), the "Agent tool has no effort parameter" claim (lines 122-123) and the "Haiku's 200K context is hard" rule (lines 207-209) are directly contradicted. The effort-index arithmetic and "40-50%" saving in the closing section, the "5x cheaper" retry example, and the Opus-5-priced dollar figures and 0.1x cache-read rate (lines 97-102) are all derived from superseded models and prices.

The tier-addressing, turn-cap and barrier guidance, the inspector/drafter sonnet-high and worker sonnet-medium claims, model-scoped caches, and the inherit-means-session-model point are confirmed by the facts file and should survive. The mechanical tier is also under-specified: its triage sketch and prose never set an effort, so it runs at the session's effort.
critic_summary: The first pass was thorough on the headline stale claims (the L30, L121-122, L207 and L213 contradictions, and the L463-464 derived percentages). It missed the L123 conclusion derived from the false 'Agent tool has no effort' premise, the $33 figure at L102 computed from Opus 5 prices, and two keep markers, and it misclassified two of its own findings (L99, L367).
